title: Sprint 2 — Product Trust
description: Improve MIA from MVP into trustworthy AI sales assistant. Customer memory, persistent corrections, assistant lifecycle audit, conversation intelligence, AI context quality.

classification.rationale: Classified as COMPLEX complexity. Complexity drivers: 30 files affected, schema changes required, AI behaviour changes, security implications, cross-cutting (multi-domain), category requires council. Required agents (10): architect, database, backend, frontend, ai_engineer, performance, security, qa, release, memory_engineer.

decisions.rationale: Approved. Sprint 2 addresses critical trust gap — customer memory, correction persistence, and AI context quality are essential for product credibility. No strategic concerns.
Approved. Architecture impact is moderate — customer memory uses existing tables, no new vectors. Assistant lifecycle audit is analysis-only. Conversation intelligence extends existing patterns.
Approved. Customer memory aligns with domain model (customers + conversations + messages). Persistent corrections connect learning events → knowledge. No domain boundary violations.
Approved. These features directly address user trust: MIA remembering customers, learning from corrections, and providing useful conversation context. High value, moderate complexity.
Approved. Customer memory analysis first, schema changes minimal. No new tables anticipated — leverage existing customers, conversations, messages, assistant_memory, learning_events.
Approved. New API surface needed: customer memory CRUD, correction persistence, conversation search/filter. Existing patterns to follow.
Approved. Conversation page enhancements (search, filters, status). New customer memory panel. Reuse existing component patterns.
Approved. AI context quality audit is critical — need to verify what reaches the model. Customer memory injection into prompts. No hardcoded prompts.
Approved. Customer memory queries should be indexed by customer_id + business_id. No premature optimization needed.
Approved. Customer data isolation critical. Memory must be scoped to business. No cross-business leakage. RLS policies must cover new memory data.
Approved. Quality gates: lint, build, Playwright tests, DevTools check. Sprint 2 validation report required.
Approved. All governance artifacts must be committed. Atomic commits per phase.
Approved. Engineering memory must record: architecture decisions, schema changes, correction flow design, security audit.
